text:
morgan: Quick docs PR coordination — need to finalize SDK snippets across py/ts/go for streaming + retries + pagination. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123. Root cause: rename of resume token field and retry config shape changed (old `max_retries` -> new `retry.max_attempts`, plus `retry.backoff_ms`). Want one unified porting note + short samples for each language. Goal: land by EOD Wed.

jess: on it — will review the Python examples and add a tiny tests asserting resume token round-trip.

sri: I'll take TS. Heads up: TS client now returns an AsyncIterable of chunks (each item {chunk, resume_token}) instead of EventEmitter; example should use `for await (...)`. Will draft.

dave: I'll handle Go snippet. Go SDK exposes a `Stream` that returns an iterator-like object with `Next()` and `ResumeToken()`. I'll add a short example that uses context timeouts and shows resumption.

morgan: also need to update any docs that still say `max_retries` — search pattern `max_retries` across repo. I left a TODO comment in examples.md line ~130.

sam: docs-bot linkcheck flagged 1 broken link in examples.md:132 — I fixed it in a tiny branch and will rebase onto this PR.

jess: quick python question: prefer `async with client.stream(...) as s:` or `async for chunk in client.stream(...)`? I think show `async for` as canonical pattern, but include the `async with` comment for context managers.

sri: agree — TS will only show the async iterator (keep surface area small). We should avoid showing multiple streaming APIs across examples.

dave: Go will be explicit with loop and `io.EOF`. Example I'll push: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()
s, err := client.Stream(ctx, params)
for {
  chunk, err := s.Next()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
  fmt.Println(chunk.Text)
}
token := s.ResumeToken()
// save token for resume: client.Stream(ctx, {resume_token: token})
```

morgan: also add a short paragraph about idempotency: clients auto-retry idempotent requests; non-idempotent calls should set `idempotency_key`. Put that in the porting guide.

sam: pushed minor lint fixes and renamed snippet path to `snippets/streaming/py_ts_go_porting/` per config. Preview deploy updated.

docs-bot: deploy preview for PR 4123 is live: https://deploy-preview-4123--docs.redwood.ai ✅

jess: I'm adding a small py test under `docs-tests/snippets_test.py` that does:
```py
async def test_resume_roundtrip(tmp_path, client):
    # start a stream, collect first chunk, get token, resume and compare
    async for part in client.stream(params):
        token = part.resume_token
        break
    resumed = []
    async for part in client.stream({**params, 'resume_token': token}):
        resumed.append(part)
    assert len(resumed) > 0
```

sri: I'll add a minimal jest test that asserts `for await` yields chunks and `chunk.resume_token` exists.

dave: I'm adding a short note in Go section explaining safe resume semantics (server guarantees at-least-once for resumed ranges; include caveat for non-idempotent side effects).

morgan: assigning reviewers: @jess @sri @dave — please approve or leave NAK with suggested snippet updates before EOD Wed. If blocked ping me. 🙏

jess: ack — aiming to finish review by tomorrow morning.

sri: ack, will drop a patch with TS snippet + jest test today.

dave: ack, will open a tiny go snippet commit and link in the PR.

sam: if anyone needs me to squash commits or handle merge conflicts I can take that after reviews.

morgan: thanks all — once merged I'll add an entry to the changelog under "Docs: SDK snippet porting (streaming/resume/retry)" and notify integrators.

jess: small nit — in python code examples use `retry.max_attempts` and `retry.backoff_ms` examples like `retry={"max_attempts": 3, "backoff_ms": 200}` so readers can copy/paste.

sri: noted. Also I'll update the TypeScript snippet to show `retry: { maxAttempts: 3, backoffMs: 200 }` to match the new SDK camelCase.

docs-bot: CI: docs-lint: passed, linkcheck: passed after sam's fix.

morgan: awesome — if no blockers, I'll merge on Wednesday and tag release notes. 🎉
